voyage.name: Palazzo Reale
voyage.content: The Palace was built in the 16th century, modernised in the 17th and converted to a museum in 1946. The result is a wacky hybrid of medieval, baroque and bling. You enter via the palace gardens to reach the ticket office. The ticket covers five attractions:- Galleria Sabauda houses the vast art collection of the rulers of Savoy.- Chapel of the Shroud is accessed this way, and from a gallery looks into the Cathedral.-

voyage.name: Museo Civico d'Arte Antica
voyage.content: This museum is within Palazzo Madama on Piazza Castello. It's misnamed, as the art collection is Gothic, Renaissance and Baroque, and more ancient (eg Byzantine) work is elsewhere.

voyage.name: CAMERA – Italian Centre for Photography
voyage.content: Impressive quality photography, with 3 or 4 exhibitions a year.

voyage.name: Museo Egizio
voyage.content: "The road to Memphis and Thebes passes through Turin" said Egyptologist Jean-François Champollion about Museo Egizio in Turin, second only in order of importance to the one in Cairo. Many artifacts were collected by Bernardino Drovetti (1776 - 1852) when he was consul of France in Egypt. In 1824, King Carlo Felice di Savoia purchased the diplomat's entire collection and housed it in the palace built in the 17th centu

voyage.name: Risorgimento Museum
voyage.address: Palazzo Carignano, Via Accademia delle Scienze 5
voyage.content: Fascinating exposition of the tumultuous birth of modern Italy, set in the very building where many events took place: Carlo Alberto and Vittorio Emanuele II were born here, and the first Italian parliament sat here. Garibaldi's campaign was in the context of revolutions and upheavals all over Europe, the greatest of all being the Industrial Revolution. It was a very literary and graphic age, so events are vividly sh

voyage.name: Galleria d'Italia
voyage.content: Galleria d'Italia is a museum chain to show off the art owned by Intesa Sanpaolo bank, the modern nobility. The Turin branch, opened in 2022, is in the Palazzo Turinetti di Pertengo and mostly displays photography. Their others are in Milan, Naples and Vicenza.

voyage.name: Foundation Accorsi-Ometto
voyage.content: Extensive display of furniture, painting and other decorative art.

voyage.name: Museo Regionale di Scienze Naturali
voyage.content: Trad natural history display of rocks and stuffed animals in a former hospital.

voyage.name: Galleria Civica d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea
voyage.content: Huge permanent collection of 19th and 20th century art.

voyage.name: Mole Antonelliana
voyage.content: The Mole, Turin's landmark building built in 1888, was intended as a synagogue but the size and cost got out of hand and the Jewish community never used it. The 167.5-metre tower is the highest work of masonry in Europe and you can ride a lift to the cupola at the top. Within it, the National Cinema Museum is a vast exhibition space spiralling up five floors. The themes of the floors are the archaeology of cinema, th

voyage.name: Museo Nazionale dell'Automobile
voyage.content: The collection houses over 170 vehicles, from 18th-century carriages to Formula 1 racers, and lots of gorgeous red sports cars.

voyage.name: Museum of Criminal Anthropology
voyage.content: Cesare Lombroso (1835-1909) was convinced that criminality was inherited, little influenced by environment and that criminals could be distinguished by their ugly atavistic features. It therefore followed that any ethnic group that didn't fit Italian concepts of beauty was inferior and should be subjugated. And women should be subjugated by men, as their much lower rate of criminal offending proved that, um, well any

voyage.name: Museo Nazionale della Montagna Duca degli Abruzzi
voyage.content: History of alpine mountaineering.

voyage.name: Museum of The New Prison
voyage.content: Spooky museum of prisons and punishments. Visit by guided tour; booking is recommended, and essential for the descent into the air raid shelter.

voyage.name: Museum of Oriental Art
voyage.content: This museum houses art from Kandahar, India, Southeast Asia, China and Japan. The third floor shows Buddhist and Tibetan culture. The fourth floor is Islamic and Arabian, mainly bronzes, ceramics and tiles.

voyage.name: Museum of the Shroud
voyage.content: The original Sindone or Turin Shroud is in safekeeping in the Cathedral and rarely displayed. This small museum displays a copy and studies the Shroud. It's a remarkable object whatever it is, a 4.4 x 1.1 m winding sheet charred by fire and appearing to bear the likeness of a man, matching the Gospel description of the crucifixion of Jesus. Multiple tests have produced contradictory results, or at least contradictory

voyage.name: Palazzo Barolo
voyage.content: Baroque bling palace, visit by guided tour. Its last private owner Carlo Tancredi Falletti di Barolo served Napoleon then worked tirelessly for relief of the poor; his palace then became an opera house.

voyage.name: Pietro Micca Museum
voyage.content: In 1706 the French besieged Turin for four months as part of the War of Spanish Succession, which embroiled all major European powers and their colonies. The defending Savoyards had dug 15 km of counter-sapping tunnels, to prevent the French burrowing in. That meant the French could only attack ineffectively from a distance. Pietro Micca sacrificed himself in detonating a tunnel that they were breaking into; a few da

voyage.name: Pinacoteca Giovanni e Marella Agnelli
voyage.content: Striking modern building, maybe an orbiter's solar power module? - perched atop the Lingotti Centre. It houses the Agnelli's private art collection, with many big names represented.

voyage.name: Museo Lavazza
voyage.content: All about coffee and the Lavazza brand, in a former coffee factory.

voyage.name: Museo Ettore Fico
voyage.content: Only open for temporary exhibitions, but with a small permanent display of the work of Ettore Fico (1917-2004).

voyage.name: Fondazione Sandretto Re Rebaudengo
voyage.content: Art exhibition gallery in a former automobile factory and outdoor sculpture park.

voyage.name: MACA
voyage.content: Science museum, child-oriented, limited English signage.

voyage.name: Cathedral of Saint John the Baptist
voyage.alt: Duomo; Cattedrale di San Giovanni Battista
voyage.content: Large elegant cathedral dating from late 15th century, enlarged in the 17th to create the Chapel for the Shroud of Turin. However this chapel (rebuilt after a fire in 1997) is nowadays accessed as part of a tour of Palazzo Reale and can't be seen from the Cathedral; visit the nearby Sindone Museum to see a copy of the Shroud.

voyage.name: Chapel of the Merchants
voyage.alt: Cappella dei Mercanti, Negozianti e Banchieri
voyage.content: A jewel of baroque architecture and sacred art built from 1680 by businessmen anxious to sanctify their dealings - they were, let's stress, "The Pious Congregation of Bankers, Shopkeepers and Merchants of Turin." One theme of the decor is the Magi, bearing the trade valuables without which the Christian church couldn't exist. The chapel was created within Chiesa dei Santi Martiri, a 16th-century Jesuit church. Its be

voyage.name: Santa Maria di Monte dei Cappuccini
voyage.content: A late-Renaissance-style church on a hill overlooking the River Po. It was built 1583 to 1656 for the Capuchin Friars; the delay was through plague and the occasional war. A miracle supposedly occurred in 1640 during the French assault on Turin, when troops seizing the church were repulsed by a sheet of holy flame from the tabernacle. They slew all the defenders anyhow, no doubt in a faith-affirming sort of way. Cann

voyage.name: Basilica di Maria Ausiliatrice
voyage.alt: Basilica of Our Lady Help of Christians
voyage.content: Palladian church built 1865-68, originally as part of a care facility for poor and delinquent boys founded by Don Bosco (1815-88). He himself is buried here, along with 6000 bits and pieces of saints.

voyage.name: Parrocchia Sacro Cuore di Maria
voyage.content: Neo-gothic church of 1890.

voyage.name: Chiesa Maria Santissima Del Carmelo
voyage.content: This church was built in the 1730s for a Carmelite convent.

voyage.name: Santuario della Consolata
voyage.alt: Church of the Virgin of the Consolation
voyage.content: A church and Benedictine monastery may have stood here since the 5th century. Most of it is from 1680 to 1740, an over-the-top profusion of baroque.

voyage.name: San Lorenzo
voyage.content: This church was built from 1634 by Guarino Guarini to a complex baroque design, where square basilica plan and Grecian cross segues into circular, octagonal and elliptical forms. This creates a striking light-play, especially in the dome, which Guarini might not be pleased to know is dubbed faccia del diavolo, the face of the devil.

voyage.name: Chiesa della Gran Madre di Dio
voyage.content: A neo-classical miniature pantheon at the far end of Vittorio Emanuele I bridge, closing off the view down Via Po. It was built to celebrate the defeat of Napoleon and return of the Savoy monarchy in 1814, but only completed in 1831.

voyage.name: Mausoleo della Bela Rosin
voyage.content: Rosa Vercellana (1833-1885) became the mistress of the future Victor Emmanuel II and had two children by him before she was 16. She was made a countess when his legitimate wife and queen died in 1855, and in 1869 when the king thought he himself might die, he hurriedly married Rosa. It was a morganatic marriage, so it conferred no crown or right of succession on her or her children. He survived to do the same thing o

voyage.name: Botanic Museum
voyage.content: Small collection and somewhat run down.

voyage.name: La Venaria Reale
voyage.content: Built as a royal hunting lodge from 1675, this grew and grew into a humonguous bling palace, trying to outshine Versailles. It became a barracks and was knocked about in Napoleonic times, remaining military until the 1930s, then the vandals set about it. Restoration was piecemeal until 1996, then a ten-year project brought it back to its former baroque opulence. Highlights include the Salone di Diana, the Galleria Gr

voyage.name: La Mandria
voyage.address: Viale Carlo Emanuele II 256, Venaria Reale
voyage.content: The "hunting lodge" grew into such a vast palace that what was needed was a new hunting lodge. However, King Victor Emmanuel II needed somewhere to ensconce his mistress La Bela Rosin, so this new lodge in turn became so big and blinged up that . . . life can be really tough when you're a plutocrat monarch. Wild boar, deer and rare breeds of horse roam the park, which has multiple access points. In the 20th century i

voyage.name: Basilica of Superga
voyage.content: This hilltop basilica was built in thanksgiving for the 1706 defeat of the French at Turin. Often incorrectly called a cathedral, it's in sort-of-classical-with-baroque style, and houses the tombs of many nobles of the House of Savoy. Superga hill derives its name from Serrapergia meaning "mountain between the hills". Nearby is a monument to the air crash of 1949, which wiped out Torino FC. Get here by car, bus, rack

voyage.name: Infini.to
voyage.content: Two shows midweek and three at weekends, only in Italian.

voyage.name: Villa della Regina
voyage.content: A royal palace and gardens on a hill east edge of the city. It's modest by Savoyard standards but plush with Chinese and Baroque interiors. This reflects the era of Anne Marie d'Orléans, in residence from 1692. Next to the Villa, the Queen's vineyard has been productive since the 1600s, and its "Freisa di Chieri DOC - Villa della Regina" red wine is on sale here.

voyage.name: Moncalieri Castle
voyage.content: This castle was built as a fortress by Thomas I of Savoy, but enlarged into a pleasure palace in the mid-15th century. From the 19th century it was especially used by queen mothers and princesses. Today it houses the Carabinieri, though the castle and its apartments can be visited. Reservation required.

voyage.name: Palazzina di Caccia di Stupinigi
voyage.content: Royal hunting lodge built from 1729, and like Veneria Reale its embellishments then got out of hand to create something a Disney princess would swoon over, grand halls and galleries and salons with putti and nymphs in industrial quantities. It houses a huge collection of Piedmontese furniture in its Rococo interiors. Outside is the Parco naturale, the hunting park and gardens, but Fritz the resident elephant has long

voyage.name: Zoom Torino
voyage.content: Spacious zoo exhibiting animals from around the world.

voyage.name: Castello di Rivoli
voyage.content: The hilltop castle was built around 900 AD but from the 17th century had so many incomplete extensions, abandoned or wrecked by the French, that owners and architects risked being driven mad. One who did go mad was King Victor Amadeus II (1666-1732), who horrified noble society by publicly marrying his mistress here; he was deposed and incarcerated within the castle to stop him declaring war on Milan or Poland or hea

voyage.name: Teatro Regio
voyage.content: The city opera house is active Oct-June. It was opened in 1740 but burned down in 1936. Reconstruction took until 1973, with a modern building behind the original facade, seating 1500.

voyage.name: Teatro Carignano
voyage.content: The city's oldest and premier theatre, opened in 1753. It was wrecked by fire in 1786 but swiftly rebuilt to the original plan, and from 1936 to 1973 it was the opera house during Teatro Regio's lengthy closure.

voyage.name: Teatro Colosseo
voyage.content: A modern concert hall seating 1500.

voyage.name: Juventus FC
voyage.content: "Juve", founded in 1897, play soccer in Serie A, Italy's top tier, and have almost never been out of the top flight. Allianz Stadium, capacity 41,000, has a club museum.

voyage.name: Torino FC
voyage.address: Stadio Olimpico Grande Torino, Via Filadelfia
voyage.content: "Toro" also play in Serie A. The original club was founded in 1906 and dominated until 1949, when team and staff died in the Superga air crash. They had mixed fortunes thereafter and went bust in 2005, so this is a phoenix club. The stadium, capacity 28,000, was built in the 1930s and renovated for the 2006 Winter Olympics, and for some obscure reason is no longer named for Benito Mussolini.

voyage.name: Porta Palazzo
voyage.content: Big street and indoor market for food produce, clothes, houseware, ethnic products, handicrafts and second-hand articles. On the second Sunday of each month there's a smaller antiques and flea market called Gran Balôn.

voyage.name: Grom
voyage.content: Renowned ice cream chain. Their other outlets are on Via Accademia delle Scienze, Via Garibaldi, Corso Romania and Via Nizza.

voyage.name: Piola Cianci
voyage.content: Popular place for fast inexpensive antipasti and main meals.

voyage.name: Focacceria Lagrange
voyage.content: Nice place to eat light and crispy focaccia. Fast service. Mostly takeaway but they have a few tables inside and out.

voyage.name: Gofreria Piemontèisa
voyage.content: Gofri are waffles Piedmont style, thin with sweet or savoury fillings.

voyage.name: La Stuzzicheria
voyage.content: Good local good pizza and excellent farinata.

voyage.name: Bicyclette
voyage.content: Impressive variety of sweet and savory crepes; high quality dough and ingredients.

voyage.name: Pizzeria Ristorante Gonzales Torino
voyage.content: Simple local pizzeria, can feel crowded and grubby.

voyage.name: Kipling
voyage.content: Reliable mix of trad Italian and international fare.

voyage.name: Caffè Mulassano
voyage.content: Charming atmospheric cafe on the main square.

voyage.name: Baratti & Milano
voyage.content: Elegant cafe on the main square, founded in 1858.

voyage.name: Lobelix
voyage.content: This bar serves a nightly aperitivo - your drink buys access to the food, which runs out towards 21:00.

voyage.name: Gennaro Esposito
voyage.content: Offbeat design and combos, excellent Neapolitan pizza.

voyage.name: Fratelli La Cozza
voyage.content: Pizzeria and seafood. Try for a balcony seat for views down the boulevard.

voyage.name: L'Acino
voyage.content: Hearty Piedmont cuisine.

voyage.name: Il Giglio
voyage.content: Serving quality seafood.

voyage.name: Tre Galli
voyage.content: Relaxing place for Piedmontese fare or just a drink.

voyage.name: Sfashion Cafè
voyage.content: Pizzeria and south Italian dishes in kitsch jazzy surroundings. It's owned by Piero Chiambretti (b 1956) the TV entertainer and presenter.

voyage.name: Gelateria Pepino
voyage.content: An ice-cream parlor founded in 1884. They were personal favorites of Benito Mussolini, and during his regime Pepino sent daily ice-cream deliveries to the dictator in Rome.

voyage.name: Caffè San Carlo
voyage.content: Glitzy cafe with upscale meals.

voyage.name: Da Mauro
voyage.content: Good reviews for their home cooking. Great value for money, come early or you won't get in.

voyage.name: Birichin
voyage.content: Gourmet restaurant with wide selection of Italian fare and huge wine selection, mostly good reviews.

voyage.name: Arcadia
voyage.content: Beautiful place with Italian and Japanese cuisine. The Japanese is just sushi and bento-box offerings, stick to the Italian.

voyage.name: Caffè Fiorio
voyage.content: Swanky old-style cafe for desserts and ice cream, several reviewers felt the quality and service didn't live up to the decor.

voyage.name: Trattoria Ala
voyage.content: Tuscan fare, so wild boars enter here at their peril.

voyage.name: Spada Reale
voyage.content: Restaurant with Piedmontese, Tuscan and Sicilian offerings.

voyage.name: Trattoria Imbianchini & Decoratori
voyage.content: Piemontese and other north Italian cuisine.

voyage.name: La Livella
voyage.content: Stylish restaurant with moderate prices.

voyage.name: Trattoria San Domenico
voyage.content: Traditional Italian food, with Sardinian specialities.

voyage.name: Pizzeria Due Torri
voyage.content: Good pizza and pasta dishes. Friendly efficient staff.

voyage.name: Antica Bruschetteria Pautasso
voyage.content: Specialises in local Piedmont dishes, including bagna cauda.

voyage.name: Osteria del Frate
voyage.content: Good food in Piedmontese style, friendly staff.

voyage.name: Mezzaluna
voyage.price: Antipasti for €7, primi and secondi for €12
voyage.content: Friendly staff serving vegan versions of Italian and other dishes.

voyage.name: Porto di Savona
voyage.content: High quality Piedmont cuisine.

voyage.name: Ristorante Del Cambio
voyage.content: A posh restaurant serving Piemontese delicacies, occasional flops but mostly great reviews. They even offer a tasting menu for vegetarians. You want to be in the palatial main dining salon not in Farmacia cafe or Cavour bar.

voyage.name: Mare Nostrum
voyage.content: Excellent southern Italian and Sicilian seafood fish dishes. The starter is a must, just one entry on the menu, but you receive six small dishes of the day.

voyage.name: Piano35
voyage.content: This teeters atop a skyscraper designed by Renzo Piano, occupied by Intesa Sanpaolo Bank. High scores for food and service, and you're paying for the rooftop view.

voyage.name: Caffe al Bicerin
voyage.content: Home of the classic Torinese drink, the Bicerin, a mix of coffee, hot chocolate and cream. But pricey and long queues.

voyage.name: Birrificio Torino
voyage.content: Brewpub restaurant with six beers brewed on premises. Good menu with recommended matched beers. More restaurant than pub, it can be very busy.

voyage.name: Caffe Rossini
voyage.content: Calls itself a restaurant, but it's really a café and late-night pub with music and a young crowd.

voyage.name: Lab Vittorio
voyage.content: Small lively bar with good cocktails and tapas. They have another bar at Via Mazzini 5.

voyage.name: Casa Romar
voyage.content: Simple pensione, rooms are en suite but on upper floors with no lift. Good transport to city centre and free parking.

voyage.name: Hotel Nizza
voyage.content: Basic but decent-value hotel next to the station. All rooms en suite with air-con. Pets are welcome.

voyage.name: Hotel Bologna
voyage.content: Central location, good value and friendly staff. No breakfast facilities.

voyage.name: Hotel Due Mondi
voyage.content: A bit shabby, but good location and fair value for money.

voyage.name: Holiday Inn Turin - Corso Francia
voyage.content: Boxy, modern well-furnished hotel. Underground parking.

voyage.name: Hotel Artua'&Solferino
voyage.content: Creaky but central pensione by Re Umberto parking lot.

voyage.name: Le Petit Hotel
voyage.content: Clean mid-price hotel near Piazza Solferino. No aircon.

voyage.name: Hotel Diplomatic
voyage.content: Tired old hotel but convenient for Porta Susa station.

voyage.name: Boston Art Hotel
voyage.content: Mid-price hotel just south of historical centre, rooms are plain, tired and worn.

voyage.name: NH Lingotto Congress
voyage.content: Business hotel in a former Fiat Lingotto factory. Large high-ceilinged rooms, with a rooftop race-track.

voyage.name: Hotel Victoria
voyage.content: Charming central hotel with spa and oriental theme.

voyage.name: NH Santo Stefano
voyage.content: Great location opposite Palazzo Reale in historic centre, this hotel gets good reviews for rooms and service. Also has a beautiful spa.

voyage.name: Grand Hotel Sitea
voyage.content: Rooms well appointed, and well serviced. Good restaurant, helpful staff. Short walk to Piazza San Carlo.

voyage.name: AC Hotel Torino
voyage.content: 4-star, part of Marriott chain. Good-sized, well-furnished rooms, good breakfast buffet. Parking on premises.

voyage.name: Principi di Piemonte
voyage.content: Elegant 5-star hotel in the centre of the historical district, gets great reviews for comfort, dining and service.
